title: Opaque context envelope and perf-aware sampling
creator: Asha Varma
description:
Problem:
Customer services and SDKs are emitting large sets of trace headers and free-form context keys that both leak PII and inflate network payloads. At the same time our default sampling is static which misses short bursts of high-error traffic. We need a compatibility-friendly approach that: (1) wraps and sanitizes arbitrary incoming context into an opaque envelope to avoid PII propagation; (2) exposes a stable SDK API so apps can annotate high-importance requests to bypass sampling; and (3) implements a perf-aware adaptive sampling controller that raises sampling during latency/error spikes while keeping overall volume bounded.

Goals:
- Backwards compatible: preserve trace IDs / essential propagation for legacy clients while removing noisy keys by default.
- Safety: prevent accidental PII (headers, cookies, x-* baggage) from appearing in exported spans or logs.
- Observability: surface sampling rate, envelope compression ratio, and annotation bypass counts to Console dashboards.
- Low overhead: SDK and middleware changes must add <0.5ms median overhead to request path under normal load.

Proposed approach:
1) Opaque context envelope: SDKs and middleware will collect incoming propagation headers into a single base64-encoded JSON blob stored under a single carrier key (redwood-ctx-envelope). During attachment to spans, only whitelisted keys (traceparent, tracestate, sampled, redwood-route-id) are promoted to span attributes; everything else remains inside the envelope. The envelope is truncated and hashed to limit size; full contents are stored only when a debug flag is set.
2) Sanitizer rules: configure default sanitizer blacklist (cookie, authorization, set-cookie, x-forwarded-*). Implement canonicalization and redaction rules. Provide a rule override API for platform teams.
3) Perf-aware sampling controller: a light-weight controller that subscribes to service-level latency and error-rate metrics (from local SDK histograms). When SLO breach patterns are detected (5xx spike or p95 latency > threshold) controller temporarily raises sampling multiplier for the affected route for a short, decay-based window to capture root-cause traces. Sampling decisions respect annotations: requests annotated as critical by app code set sampling priority=2 and are always kept.
4) SDK API surface: new RequestContext API with methods: wrapEnvelope(headers), annotateCritical(reason), setSamplingHint(int). Provide middleware adapters for Express, FastAPI, Spring WebFlux.
5) Telemetry & dashboards: emit metrics: redwood.sampling.rate (gauge per route), redwood.envelope.size (histogram), redwood.sampling.override.count (counter). Add Console dashboard tiles for sampling vs error/latency by route and time.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDKs for Node/Python/Java implement envelope and sanitizer and pass the compatibility integration suite.
- Sampling controller reduces missed-error traces in synthetic failure test by >=60% without exceeding baseline trace volume by >40%.
- End-to-end tests verifying that redwood-ctx-envelope contains sanitized keys and PII is absent in exported spans.
- Performance tests show median per-request overhead <0.5ms at 95th percentile for single core.

Out of scope:
- Full-proof dynamic sampling ML models (future work).
- Long-term storage of raw envelopes for more than debug window.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Using a single envelope key simplifies header explosion across proxies and reduces telemetry cardinality, but adds an encoding step per request. We mitigate cost with fast base64 and optional in-memory dedupe.
- Always-on annotation bypass lets product teams mark important flows; we will require gating for high-traffic routes to prevent data explosion.

Next steps:
- Finalize sanitizer default list and QA checklist with security.
- Implement Node SDK prototype and middleware shim.
- Create synthetic failure tests and dashboards in Console staging.
